item.title: Ukrainian foreign minister says Russian-held town is a 'death trap' with starving residents
item.description: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Saturday that Russian occupying forces were turning the Ukrainian town of Oleshky into a "death trap" gripped by starvation, and urged international organisations to help evacuate its residents.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Saturday that Russian occupying forces were turning the Ukrainian town of Oleshky into a "death trap" gripped by starvation, and urged international organisations to help evacuate its residents. Sybiha made his comments on X a day after Russian President Vladimir Putin pledged, in a [USN:L8N4621IK TEXT:"conversation with Pope Leo"], to cooperate in delivering vital supplies into the town in southern Ukraine's Kherson region. "Russians are trying to turn the Ukrainian town of Oleshky into a death trap. The hospital has run out of medicine. Dozens of bodies lie in the streets or in homes, as Russians forbid residents from burying them," Sybiha wrote. "Families are starving, surviving on leftover garden vegetables, preserves and even snails ... Ukraine has repeatedly called for safe evacuation and international humanitarian access. These appeals cannot remain unanswered." The Kremlin acknowledged in September that Oleshky had [USN:R4N45100U TEXT:"critical problems"] with food and medical supplies but said Russia's military was working to resolve them. Ukraine's military has twice used drones to [USN:L1N45Q03T TEXT:"deliver food"] and medicine to the town. Sybiha urged the United Nations, the International Committee of the Red Cross and other organisations to "secure safe evacuation corridors and immediate humanitarian access." Oleshky lies on the east side of the Dnipro River in Kherson region, which Russian forces mostly occupied soon after the 2022 invasion. A Ukrainian counteroffensive later recaptured large chunks of territory, including the city of Kherson. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy described the situation in Oleshky this week as [USN:L8N45Y0E8 TEXT:""genocide.""] Oleshky had a pre-war population of 24,000 people and is now home to around 1,700 residents, including 47 children, according to Danielle Bell, head of the United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine. Local prosecutors said on Saturday Russian forces dropped aerial bombs on the city of Kherson, on the opposite bank of the Dnipro from Oleshky, killing an ambulance driver and wounding 40 people.

item.title: Muere en ataque a balazos reconocido exfiscal anticorrupción de Guatemala
item.description: El abogado guatemalteco Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa, conocido por su lucha contra la corrupción en el país centroamericano, falleció tras ser atacado el sábado a balazos por dos dos hombres cuando visitaba un centro deportivo en la capital de Guatemala, un crimen que fue condenado por el presidente Bernardo Arévalo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El abogado guatemalteco Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa, conocido por su lucha contra la corrupción en el país centroamericano, falleció tras ser atacado el sábado a balazos por dos dos hombres cuando visitaba un centro deportivo en la capital de Guatemala, un crimen que fue condenado por el presidente Bernardo Arévalo. El abogado, de 43 años, quien denunció la corrupción de empresarios y políticos, formó parte por poco tiempo en 2023 de la defensa del periodista guatemalteco [USN:L1N3Z81J8 TEXT:"José Rubén Zamora"], actualmente en arresto domiciliario, pero tuvo que dejar el caso tras ser acusado por el Ministerio Público de Consuelo Porras de obstaculizar el proceso y destruir u ocultar información. Poco después del ataque contra Solórzano Foppa, la policía informó que detuvo a dos hombres a los que les incautó un arma de fuego tipo carabina y una motocicleta. "Repudio enérgicamente el cobarde asesinato del exfiscal Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa. Sus autores, materiales e intelectuales, deben pagar las consecuencias con todo el peso de la ley", dijo el presidente Arévalo en su cuenta oficial X, y agregó que instruyó a su gobierno a coordinarse con las autoridades competentes para el esclarecimiento del crimen. "Quienes creen que el terror puede intimidar al pueblo de Guatemala y al gobierno que dirijo, se equivocan. En honor a Foppa, en honor a nuestra patria, en honor a la justicia", subrayó. El abogado se destacó por su lucha contra la corrupción cuando fue jefe de la Dirección de Investigaciones Criminalísticas en el Ministerio Público, así como cuando fungió entre 2016 y 2018 como jefe de la autoridad tributaria, SAT, cuando llevó a prisión y obligó a decenas de poderosos empresarios guatemaltecos a pagar impuestos. En 2025, Solórzano Foppa denunció una presunta vinculación entre la pandilla del Barrio 18 y el partido Unidad Nacional de la Esperanza (UNE), así como la existencia de vínculos entre las pandillas y el sistema judicial.

item.title: Nuggets G/F Julian Strawther (knee) sidelined at least six weeks
item.description: Denver Nuggets swingman Julian Strawther will miss at least six weeks after suffering a left knee sprain during a preseason game last week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Denver Nuggets swingman Julian Strawther will miss at least six weeks after suffering a left knee sprain during a preseason game last week. Strawther was injured Wednesday against the Los Angeles Clippers and helped off the court. There were fears the injury was season-ending before an MRI exam detected a sprain. Strawther will be re-examined in six weeks, when an updated timetable will likely be revealed. The 24-year-old Strawther has averaged 7.1 points and 1.8 rebounds in 172 games (18 starts) over three NBA seasons. Last season, he averaged 7.2 points and 2.0 rebounds in 57 games (14 starts) and shot a career-best 46.7% from the field. He is eligible through Monday to sign a rookie-scale extension with the Nuggets. Strawther was a first-round pick (29th overall) by Denver out of Gonzaga in 2023. --Field Level Media

item.title: Lions play through tears in honour of teammate Andrews
item.description: Several of the players from South Africa’s Lions side could not hold back tears as they paid an emotional tribute to teammate Hyron Andrews ahead of their Champions Cup fixture against French side La Rochelle on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Several of the players from South Africa’s Lions side could not hold back tears as they paid an emotional tribute to teammate Hyron Andrews ahead of their Champions Cup fixture against French side La Rochelle on Saturday. Andrews, 31, was [USN:L1N4620GN TEXT:"found unresponsive at the team’s hotel"] on the Ile de Re on Friday and could not be resuscitated. No cause of death has yet been determined. A statement from South Africa Rugby said he "died after falling at the team hotel". The Lions decided to play the fixture in honour of Andrews and put in a spirited display but went down 31-14 to the more fancied home side. La Rochelle fans had formed a guard of honour to welcome the visitors at the stadium. Andrews' number 5 jersey was laid out in front of his teammates as an impeccably observed moment of silence was held at the Stade Marcel-Deflandre. Ruan Delport, selected to play in the second row, instead wore the number 24, leaving Andrews' number free. South Africans on the La Rochelle side, Dillyn Leyds and Salmaan Moerat, presented a special number 5 jersey to Lions coach Ivan Van Rooyen, while the ground erupted into applause in the fifth minute of the match. The Lions also have two United Rugby Championship fixtures in Scotland on their European tour, at Edinburgh next Friday and Glasgow Warriors the week after.

item.title: Barcelona keep perfect LaLiga record with five-goal romp at Betis
item.description: Barcelona's LaLiga juggernaut rolled into Seville on Saturday and left with the scoreboard smoking, as the leaders beat Real Betis 5-2 to make it nine wins from nine and stretch their blistering league tally to 39 goals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Barcelona's LaLiga juggernaut rolled into Seville on Saturday and left with the scoreboard smoking, as the leaders beat Real Betis 5-2 to make it nine wins from nine and stretch their blistering league tally to 39 goals. Lamine Yamal lit the fuse with a dazzling opener before Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric Garcia and substitute Dani Olmo joined the party, while Valentin Gomez and Ez Abde replied for Betis, who played much of the second half with 10 men after Facundo Bernal was sent off for headbutting Lamine. Barca moved to 27 points, five above Atletico who won 1-0 at Espanyol, while third-placed Betis have 19 and Real Madrid sit fourth on 18 before welcoming Sevilla on Sunday, Betis manager Manuel Pellegrini made eight changes from the side that beat Porto 3-2 in the Champions League, resting several key players including Antony, Marc Bartra, Natan and Isco with a midweek European meeting against Feyenoord in mind. Yet the hosts still made Barca sweat before the visitors eventually found space, rhythm and, after Betis were reduced to 10 men, plenty of room to turn the match into another attacking exhibition. Lamine opened the scoring in the 10th minute in familiar style, gliding in from the right before whipping a left-footed strike from the edge of the box into the top corner. Betis levelled in the 27th when Pablo Fornals collected a rebound on the right and clipped a cross into the middle for Gomez, who rose highest to head past goalkeeper Joan Garcia. Barcelona reclaimed the lead in the 41st minute when Spain captain Rodri powered in a header from Fermin Lopez's corner. Betis thought they had equalised three minutes later through Gio Lo Celso's spectacular swivelling volley from outside the box, but the effort was ruled out after Cucho Hernandez was adjudged to have handled earlier in the build-up. Jesus, signed from Arsenal in the close season, had a goal disallowed for offside shortly after the break but was not kept waiting long. In the 51st, Lamine darted down the right and squared for the Brazilian to finish neatly inside the area. A minute later Abde pulled one back on the counter, sliding a low shot inside the right post, but Betis' celebrations turned sour when Bernal was shown a straight red card following a scuffle. Lamine was booked for his part in the altercation. Barcelona made it 4-2 in the 63rd minute when Alvaro Valles failed to deal with Lamine's free kick and Pau Cubarsi headed the loose ball back across goal for Garcia to tap in. Olmo completed the rout in the 81st minute, curling a right-footed shot into the top corner from outside the box. Atletico won 1-0 at Espanyol, with Baena coming off the bench to deliver the late sting in a cagey match in Barcelona. Both sides struck the post in a tight tactical contest before Atletico's substitutes combined in the 89th, Julian Alvarez bursting down the left and squaring for Baena, who drove a fierce strike into the top corner from the edge of the box.

item.title: Commanders rule out RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt, 3 others vs. 49ers
item.description: Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice all week and was ruled out Saturday for Monday night's away game against the San Francisco 49ers, coach Dan Quinn told reporters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice all week and was ruled out Saturday for Monday night's away game against the San Francisco 49ers, coach Dan Quinn told reporters. Along with Croskey-Merritt, Quinn said quarterback Marcus Mariota (knee), edge rusher Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral) and defensive lineman Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle) will not travel with the team for the game in Santa Clara, Calif. Quinn said Croskey-Merritt reinjured the groin he hurt in August. "That's harder, on the same injury," he said. "We'll work really hard to get him back." Croskey-Merritt leads the Commanders with 239 rushing yards and has two rushing touchdowns. He missed the final two preseason games with a groin injury. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Austin Ekeler (chest) are expected to share running back duties, though both have been limited in practice. Jeremy McNichols, who began the season on injured reserve with a quadriceps injury, will travel with the team and could be activated Monday. Wide receiver Stefon Diggs, who missed last Sunday's 27-27 tie against the New York Giants, practiced Saturday, along with Terry McLaurin (hamstring). The pair have combined for 32 receptions, 373 yards and four scores this season. Cornerback Trey Amos (ankle) and safety Nick Cross (illness) were full participants in practice and could return Monday. Amos has been on injured reserve, while Cross has been out since Week 2. --Field Level Media

item.title: Steelers' DK Metcalf off injury report, Pat Freiermuth added
item.description: The Pittsburgh Steelers removed one player from the injury report and added another on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Pittsburgh Steelers removed one player from the injury report and added another on Saturday. Wide receiver DK Metcalf was taken off the report by the Steelers (3-2) for Sunday's game against the host Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4). He was questionable due to an illness. Tight end Pat Freiermuth, however, was added to the injury report as questionable due to a calf injury. Metcalf, Freiermuth and running back Jaylen Warren are tied for the team lead in catches with 19. Freiermuth has a club-best four touchdown receptions to go along with 169 receiving yards, while Metcalf has 225 receiving yards and one score. --Field Level Media

item.title: City's flying start comes at a cost, with Haaland limping off
item.description: Manchester City maintained their perfect Premier League start with a 3-2 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday, but the sight of a badly limping Erling Haaland heading straight down the tunnel added another concern to those already hanging over the club.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Manchester City maintained their perfect Premier League start with a 3-2 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday, but the sight of a badly limping Erling Haaland heading straight down the tunnel added another concern to those already hanging over the club. City are appealing a ruling that they breached 114 Premier League financial rules and deny wrongdoing, but the uncertainty off the pitch has done little to disrupt them on it. Enzo Maresca's side have won seven league games from seven for their best-ever start to a Premier League season. Maresca became the first manager to win his opening seven Premier League games in charge as City bounced back from Wednesday's Champions League defeat by Paris St Germain, his first meaningful loss as City boss. Haaland struck twice after Phil Foden's first goal of the season had been cancelled out by Daizen Maeda, with the Norwegian's second his 100th non-penalty Premier League goal, reached in a record 139 appearances. He was denied a hat-trick by an offside in the build-up before Zian Flemming's stoppage-time penalty made the scoreline closer than the game felt. But victory came at a potentially heavy cost during a punishing stretch of four games in 10 days. While Maresca had made six changes to his team from Wednesday, Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O'Reilly all went off injured, while Antoine Semenyo was also limping badly at the final whistle. "Unfortunately, in 10 minutes, we had four, five players (hurt)," Maresca said. "I don't have any news at the moment." Haaland made a beeline for the tunnel rather than staying to applaud supporters, unusual for the striker, with Semenyo hobbling off not far behind. DEFIANT VOICE "I don't know (Haaland's injury)," Maresca said. "I asked him. He said that he was okay. So hopefully, it's nothing serious." The uncertainty surrounding City has hardly dampened the mood among their supporters, who were in defiant voice at the Etihad as a stadium-record 60,817 watched the game. They loudly booed the Premier League anthem before kick-off and waved inflatable bananas, reviving a City tradition dating from their days outside the top flight in the 1980s. Supporters turned the prospect of possible relegation as a sanction into gallows humour, chanting "You're going down with the City!" at the travelling Ipswich fans. Outside the stadium, vendors did brisk business selling bananas and T-shirts carrying anti-charge slogans, including "Stick your charges where the sun don't shine" and "City til I die." "The environment was very good," Maresca said. "They just said to me that today was a record attendance, so that's also a nice thing. The fans, the club, the players, we are all together in this journey, and this is the best feeling for everyone." Maresca has said several times since the team reconvened after the international break that he has instructed his players to shut out external criticism as the club appeals the guilty verdict. Captain Ruben Dias said earlier in the week that "it's almost impossible to avoid seeing something, even us being as private as we can be and just doing our own lives on your phone. It's impossible to avoid everything." Maresca praised his players for their focus. "The players, they need to be worried about people inside the club and about me for the credit I give to them, and they are not worried about people that can judge them from outside. "But inside, I promise you that the players they are happy. The club gives credit to the players. I give credit to the players. So this is for us the most important thing." Asked about managing against City with everything that has happened off the pitch, Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil shrugged and said: "No. Just us against City trying to win. Bananas, no bananas, makes no difference."

item.title: Trump culpa assessores conforme pioram perspectivas dos republicanos para eleições de meio de mandato
item.description: O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, está culpando assessores de alto escalão e estrategistas políticos pela estratégia vacilante para as eleições de meio de mandato, questionando os gastos com a campanha, criticando o redesenho dos distritos eleitorais e questionando as escolhas dos candidatos, enquanto os republicanos lutam para manter o controle do Congresso, afirmaram três pessoas a par das discussões internas.
item.dc:creator: Nandita Bose, Bo Erickson, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, está culpando assessores de alto escalão e estrategistas políticos pela estratégia vacilante para as eleições de meio de mandato, questionando os gastos com a campanha, criticando o redesenho dos distritos eleitorais e questionando as escolhas dos candidatos, enquanto os republicanos lutam para manter o controle do Congresso, afirmaram três pessoas a par das discussões internas. Trump não está na cédula eleitoral de 3 de novembro, mas diz repetidamente aos apoiadores para fingirem que ele está, na esperança de mobilizar eleitores que, de outra forma, poderiam deixar de votar. Ele embarcou em uma agenda frenética de campanha, ao mesmo tempo em que evita, em grande parte, reconhecer seu próprio papel na definição da estratégia e como sua impopularidade está pesando sobre os candidatos republicanos em disputas acirradas. Grande parte do atrito tem se concentrado em James Blair, o assessor de longa data que dirige o super PAC de Trump, o MAGA Inc., e na chefe de gabinete da Casa Branca, Susie Wiles, que até agora havia escapado em grande parte das críticas. Trump criticou a forma como Blair administra os fundos de campanha, enquanto alguns funcionários da Casa Branca e aliados questionaram a supervisão de Wiles sobre a operação política. Enquanto Trump questiona por que os gastos com a campanha não conseguiram melhorar os números das pesquisas dos republicanos, seus assessores também estão se culpando mutuamente. Wiles apontou Blair, enquanto Blair culpou a equipe de assuntos legislativos da Casa Branca, disse uma das pessoas. “O que está realmente acontecendo é um ‘pelotão de fuzilamento circular’”, disse a fonte. As pesquisas de opinião sugerem que os democratas conquistarão a Câmara dos Deputados, enquanto a disputa pelo Senado continua acirrada demais para se prever o resultado. Perder a Câmara prejudicaria a agenda legislativa de Trump nos dois últimos anos de seu mandato e daria aos democratas o poder de intimar testemunhas para investigar seu governo. Trump defendeu Wiles na sexta-feira, chamando-a de “inteligente” e “dura” e afirmando que ela permaneceria no cargo. “Susie está aqui e vai ficar aqui por muito tempo”, disse ele. O porta-voz da Casa Branca, Davis Ingle, rejeitou a caracterização dada pelas fontes, dizendo que se tratavam de “especialistas de poltrona divulgando suas especulações infundadas”. Wiles não respondeu a um pedido de comentário. TRUMP HÁ MUITO TEMPO SE DISTANCIA DE REVESES POLÍTICOS Trump há muito tempo busca se distanciar de reveses políticos. Ele se recusou a aceitar sua derrota nas eleições de 2020 e afirmou, antes dos resultados das eleições intermediárias de 2022, que merecia “todo o crédito” se os republicanos vencessem, mas “não deveria ser culpado de forma alguma” se perdessem. Mais recentemente, ele lembrou ao público que o partido do presidente costuma enfrentar dificuldades nas eleições intermediárias. Mas Trump ajudou a elaborar e impulsionar algumas das estratégias que agora questiona, incluindo o esforço de redistritamento e as escolhas de candidatos moldadas por suas lealdades pessoais ou queixas. O índice de aprovação de Trump está no ponto mais baixo de sua presidência, prejudicado pela preocupação dos eleitores com os preços altos e pela insatisfação com a guerra contra o Irã. US$200 MILHÕES E REDISTRIBUIÇÃO ELEITORAL Com Trump questionando por que as pesquisas dos republicanos em disputas decisivas não melhoraram, apesar dos gastos de campanha da MAGA Inc. -- que, segundo registros públicos, somam US$200 milhões até o momento --, ainda não está claro se ele aprovará mais gastos antes da eleição, disse uma das fontes. Trump também pressionou assessores políticos e consultores na última semana para que explicassem por que a iniciativa de redistribuição distrital que ele promoveu pessoalmente não conseguiu gerar ganhos republicanos mais evidentes, disseram duas fontes. O Texas é uma preocupação especial. Os republicanos redesenharam o mapa eleitoral do Estado para ganhar cadeiras, mas a estratégia depende, em parte, de que os eleitores hispânicos compareçam às urnas como fizeram na eleição de 2024. Pesquisas de opinião sugerem que esse apoio pode ser difícil de repetir em meio a preocupações com o custo de vida e com a forma como Trump tem conduzido a economia. Alguns republicanos temem que os novos limites eleitorais possam sair pela culatra, deixando os candidatos à reeleição mais vulneráveis, em vez de dar vantagem ao partido. “O redesenho distrital fragmentou demais os eleitores de Trump”, disse uma das fontes. Trump havia dito que Blair deveria retornar à Casa Branca após as eleições de meio de mandato, descrevendo sua saída como uma “breve licença”. Mas duas fontes afirmaram que seu retorno agora é improvável. “Ele não vai voltar. Isso não vai acontecer”, disse uma delas. Não estava tão claro como as coisas se desenrolariam para Wiles, que desempenhou um papel central na vitória de Trump em 2024 e a quem os aliados e assessores de Trump atribuem o mérito de ter trazido maior disciplina à Casa Branca em seu segundo mandato. Trump “pode estar incomodado com certas coisas, mas ela tem mantido essa máquina funcionando de forma eficaz”, disse uma quarta fonte próxima à Casa Branca. (Reportagem de Nandita Bose, Steve Holland e Bo Erickson, em Washington; Reportagem adicional de Trevor Hunnicutt e Alexandra Ulmer)

item.title: Barcola shines as Liverpool labour to 2-1 win over Brentford
item.description: Liverpool bounced back from last week’s 3-0 Premier League drubbing by Manchester City with a workmanlike 2-1 win at Brentford on Saturday, as winger Bradley Barcola showcased the full range of his talents despite spurning two gilt-edged chances.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Liverpool bounced back from last week’s [USN:L8N45X08M TEXT:"3-0 Premier League drubbing by Manchester City"] with a workmanlike 2-1 win at Brentford on Saturday, as winger Bradley Barcola showcased the full range of his talents despite spurning two gilt-edged chances. Keane Lewis-Potter had given the home side the lead in the 44th minute but Yehor Yarmoliuk was sent off for an attempted headbutt deep into first-half stoppage time, and Victor Munoz and Alexander Isak completed Liverpool's comeback with second-half goals to seal the three points. "Super-happy with the win. It's a tough ground, it's a tough team to play, especially away from home. We knew it was going to be a bit of a scrappy game and it's important to come out on top," Isak said. Vitaly Janelt picked up a second yellow card in stoppage time to leave Brentford with nine men, and Barcola then squandered another opportunity when he opted to pass rather than shoot after Liverpool broke forward on the counter-attack. Perhaps his mind was still on his first-half opportunity, when he intercepted Janelt’s attempted header and raced clear, only to lift his effort over the onrushing goalkeeper and wide. Either way, the two chances gave Liverpool fans a glimpse of what may be to come once he settles fully on Merseyside. Signed from Paris St Germain in a deal [USN:L4N44Q01S TEXT:"worth up to 123 million pounds"], the 24-year-old was a constant threat from his starting position on the left wing, cutting inside onto his right foot to shoot or cross and moving infield or up front whenever the opportunity arose. With opponents often deploying five players across the back against the leading sides, Barcola’s skill, agility and trickery offer Liverpool another means of unlocking compact defences following Mohamed Salah’s departure at the end of last season. "I think there's still lots to improve. We're taking steps and we're grabbing points on the way which is important. It's a tough place to come, so three points is really good," Isak said.

item.title: Italian police clash with protesters in Milan and Bologna
item.description: Police fired tear gas on Saturday after coming under attack from protesters throwing stones in the square in front of Milan's Gothic cathedral, Italian media reported, while there were also clashes in the city of Bologna following protests over the cost of living.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Police fired tear gas on Saturday after coming under attack from protesters throwing stones in the square in front of Milan's Gothic cathedral, Italian media reported, while there were also clashes in the city of Bologna following protests over the cost of living. Police in Bologna used a water cannon to try to disperse crowds and made seven arrests after the protest became violent, the ANSA news agency reported. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, facing an election next year, condemned the violence. "Demonstrating is a right. Turning our cities into battlegrounds is not," she said on X. In Milan, police in riot gear also tried to clear hooded protesters from the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, the luxury shopping arcade on one side of the cathedral square, as groups broke away from the cost-of-living protest. Shops pulled down their shutters and tourists fled the central area. The central Duomo (Cathedral) metro station was closed during the clashes in which several people were reported injured, and arrests were made, according to the Italian media reports. The clashes echoed the violence [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"in neighbouring France,"] where tens of thousands of people, angered by rising costs and declining public services, took to the streets on Saturday in some of the country's most violent protests in years.

item.title: India, West Indies draw T20 series after rain washes out decider
item.description: India and West Indies had to settle for a 2-2 draw in their five-match T20 series after the fifth and deciding game ended with no result due to rain on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India and West Indies had to settle for a 2-2 draw in their five-match T20 series after the fifth and deciding game ended with no result due to rain on Saturday. Persistent showers delayed the start and reduced the contest to nine overs per side before West Indies won the toss and elected to field. India lost opener Abhishek Sharma for six off the bowling of Keemo Paul but Ishan Kishan then hammered 30 off 10 balls to provide the early impetus. The hosts surged to 118-5 in 7.4 overs but rain returned before the innings could be completed, forcing the players off the field. With conditions failing to improve, officials ended the match and both teams shared the series honours. The match was the first international fixture at Chinnaswamy Stadium in two years. Veteran seamer Bhuvneshwar Kumar, recalled to India's T20 squad for the first time since November 2022, was denied the chance to mark his return with the ball.

item.title: Maple Leafs F John Tavares (lower body) is week-to-week
item.description: The Toronto Maple Leafs listed forward John Tavares as week-to-week with a lower-body injury on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Toronto Maple Leafs listed forward John Tavares as week-to-week with a lower-body injury on Saturday. The designation means the 36-year-old veteran could be sidelined for up to six weeks, according to The Athletic. Tavares exited Thursday's game against Buffalo after a collision with Sabres forward Joshua Norris. Tavares has seven points (two goals, five assists) in seven games this season, his ninth with Toronto and 18th in the NHL. He has 1,192 points (527 goals, 665 assists) in 1,273 career games with the Islanders (2009-18) and Maple Leafs since New York drafted him No. 1 overall in 2009. --Field Level Media

item.title: Colts activate TE Will Mallory from IR
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts activated Will Mallory from injured reserve on Saturday, one day after they listed fellow tight end Tyler Warren as questionable with a groin injury that he sustained in practice.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Indianapolis Colts activated Will Mallory from injured reserve on Saturday, one day after they listed fellow tight end Tyler Warren as questionable with a groin injury that he sustained in practice. Mallory's questionable status was lifted from the injury report by the Colts (2-3) ahead of Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans (0-5) in Indianapolis. He had been on injured reserve since Aug. 30 with a thumb injury. Mallory, 27, has 23 catches for 252 yards in 24 career games (two starts) with the Colts. He was selected by Indianapolis in the fifth round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Miami. A Pro Bowl selection in his rookie season in 2025, Warren has 30 catches for 213 yards and two touchdowns in five games (all starts) this season. Warren, 24, also has a touchdown run. --Field Level Media

item.title: Tens of thousands march in Lisbon over housing and living costs
item.description: Tens of thousands of people marched through central Lisbon on Saturday to protest against soaring living costs and a deepening housing crisis in Portugal, increasing pressure on the centre-right government.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves, Miguel Pereira
item.content:encoded: Tens of thousands of people marched through central Lisbon on Saturday to protest against soaring living costs and a deepening housing crisis in Portugal, increasing pressure on the centre-right government. Portugal's biggest union, CGTP, which called the rally, said "many tens of thousands" packed one of the capital's main avenues. Police gave no crowd estimate. Protesters say low wages are failing to keep pace with housing costs and the rising cost of living, leaving many people struggling to make ends meet in the European Union and NATO member state. The demonstration followed days of growing unrest, including a tent camp set up by housing activists in the northern city of Porto that police cleared in a pre-dawn operation on Monday. It coincides with [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"protests in France"] against rising costs and declining public services, and smaller protests in [USN:L6N46303L TEXT:"Belgium"]. There are also mass protests in [USN:L6N46303U TEXT:"Albania"], where protesters are demanding the prime minister's resignation. Portugal's [USN:APNAL1YR5 TEXT:"inflation hit 3.6% in September"], driven by rising food and fuel prices, the latter up 15% year-on-year following an increase in tensions in the Middle East. House prices have more than doubled since 2017, while rents for new leases have nearly doubled, fuelling one of Europe's worst housing affordability crises. The squeeze is most acute in major cities. PROTESTERS' CONCERNS Carolina Cruz, 26, a PhD student and biology researcher earning about €1,300 ($1,460) a month on a scholarship, faces losing her home as her rental contract nears expiry. She and her partner pay €716 monthly for an apartment in the Lisbon area, but renewal could push the rent above €1,200 — far beyond their means. "I'm the first person in my family to enter a doctoral programme, and even with all the studying I've done, I still can't make it... Right now, housing in Lisbon is the problem," Cruz said. Pedro Penilo, 62, a teacher, said Portugal's leaders were "out of touch with reality." "Life is incredibly expensive… it's going up brutally. I need to see how my mortgage is going to turn out in the coming months, when it's adjusted. I'm very worried," he said. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Carlos Abreu Amorim said on Friday the "government will not yield to shouts from the street" and that [USN:L8N3X91P8 TEXT:"concrete measures"] to address the concerns were already being rolled out. ($1 = 0.8898 euros)

item.title: Des Palestiniens et des responsables européens attaqués par des colons en Cisjordanie occupée
item.description: Des colons juifs masqués ont attaqué des Palestiniens, des représentants de l'Eglise catholique et des responsables européens en Cisjordanie occupée, a annoncé samedi le ministre belge des Affaires étrangères.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des colons juifs masqués ont attaqué des Palestiniens, des représentants de l'Eglise catholique et des responsables européens en Cisjordanie occupée, a annoncé samedi le ministre belge des Affaires étrangères. Maxime Prévot a précisé que le consul général de Belgique, des diplomates français et polonais ainsi qu’un maire français figuraient parmi les personnes agressées, et qu’un véhicule belge avait été endommagé. "Récolter des olives, couvrir l’actualité ou exercer des fonctions diplomatiques ne devrait jamais exposer quiconque au risque d’une agression", a dénoncé le chef de la diplomatie belge. Bernard Baudoux, maire d'Aulnoye-Aymeries, dans le Nord de la France, a déclaré à Reuters qu'il récoltait des olives avec des habitants du village majoritairement chrétien de Taybeh lorsqu'il a été "violemment agressé" par des colons. "J'ai été jeté au sol", a-t-il dit. Le ministre israélien des Affaires étrangères, Gideon Sarr, a condamné l'attaque, qu'il a imputée sur la plateforme X à des "émeutiers israéliens", tout en critiquant le fait que le déplacement des responsables européens n'ait pas été coordonné avec les autorités israéliennes. Maxime Prévot a déclaré de son côté que la Belgique continuerait à faire pression pour que des sanctions soient prises à l’encontre des responsables de ces violences et de ceux qui les soutiennent. "En tant que puissance occupante, les autorités israéliennes doivent protéger les Palestiniens, garantir la sécurité des diplomates et des journalistes, et traduire les responsables en justice. Il faut mettre fin à l'impunité dont bénéficient les colons violents", a-t-il écrit sur X. Cette attaque est intervenue au lendemain de l'agression par des colons de la photo-journaliste américaine Heidi Levine, qui couvrait la récolte des olives pour le Washington Post.

item.title: Chelsea's Martinez suffered concussion after collision at Everton, says Alonso
item.description: Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez suffered a concussion after his collision with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite and was taken to hospital for "precautionary tests", manager Xabi Alonso said after their 2-0 Premier League victory.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chelsea goalkeeper Emi Martinez suffered a concussion after his collision with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite and was taken to hospital for "precautionary tests", manager Xabi Alonso said after their [USN:L1N463054 TEXT:"2-0 Premier League victory"]. Pedro Neto's double at the Hill Dickinson Stadium ended Everton's unbeaten start to the league season but Chelsea's victory was overshadowed by the lengthy injury stoppage in the second half. Martinez and Branthwaite came together when Everton's Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall whipped a free kick into the box and although the defender was back on his feet after treatment, the Argentina goalkeeper required treatment from paramedics. The 34-year-old was eventually strapped to a stretcher and carried off the field before being taken to hospital. "It was a concussion but beyond that I don't know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait," Alonso said. "What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and right now he is in hospital doing precautionary tests. We need to wait. Hopefully it won't be too bad but we need to wait." Martinez's injury forced Alonso to give Mike Penders his Premier League debut and the 21-year-old keeper helped Chelsea keep their first clean sheet in the league since January. Penders, a Belgian youth international, may have to step in for the short term due to concussion protocols preventing Martinez returning to training immediately. Chelsea host Tottenham Hotspur in the league next Saturday followed by a League Cup fourth round game at Liverpool on October 28 and a home Premier League match against Manchester United three days later. "Mike has personality. He's brave and we have full trust with him. He did well," Alonso added. "He played in the cup games and whenever he's needed, like the other players whenever they are needed they can perform. "It's all about the squad, that all the players feel important and can have their moment whenever they are needed, and that's very positive."

item.title: Guarda Revolucionária do Irã afirma que dois petroleiros atingiram minas no Estreito de Ormuz
item.description: A Marinha da Guarda Revolucionária do Irã informou neste sábado que dois petroleiros pegaram fogo após colidirem com minas navais enquanto atravessavam o Estreito de Ormuz, segundo noticiou a agência oficial de notícias iraniana Irna.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Marinha da Guarda Revolucionária do Irã informou neste sábado que dois petroleiros pegaram fogo após colidirem com minas navais enquanto atravessavam o Estreito de Ormuz, segundo noticiou a agência oficial de notícias iraniana Irna. A mídia estatal informou que ambos os petroleiros transportavam cerca de 2 milhões de barris de petróleo bruto. Não houve confirmação independente das notícias. A Irna informou que as embarcações haviam desligado seus sistemas de posicionamento e radar e tentaram usar uma rota não autorizada pela via navegável estratégica. A segunda embarcação ficou imobilizada após colidir com uma mina, acrescentou a agência. A mídia estatal havia informado anteriormente que o outro petroleiro também havia colidido com uma mina ao tentar atravessar o estreito por uma rota não autorizada pelo Irã. Os incidentes ocorrem em meio a tensões crescentes em torno do estreito, uma rota fundamental para o transporte de petróleo. As interrupções na navegação na via, decorrentes da guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã, impulsionaram os preços globais da energia e a inflação. Autoridades marítimas informaram na quarta-feira que um navio porta-contêineres e um graneleiro [USN:L1N4600JW TEXT:"afundaram"] perto do estreito após serem atingidos por projéteis em incidentes separados. [USN:L1N45U0E0 TEXT:"Os ataques"] na região da via navegável aumentaram nas últimas duas semanas, com o Irã afirmando que está intensificando os ataques em resposta ao bloqueio dos EUA aos seus portos e às sanções mais severas impostas no mês passado. (Reportagem de Menna Alaa El-Din. Reportagem adicional da redação de Dubai)

item.title: Festival crush in Indian city of Kolkata kills at least 17, local media say
item.description: A crush at a religious festival in the eastern Indian city of Kolkata killed at least 17 people and injured dozens, local media reported on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A crush at a religious festival in the eastern Indian city of Kolkata killed at least 17 people and injured dozens, local media reported on Saturday. Durga Puja, a multi-day annual Hindu festival in the state of West Bengal, draws huge crowds to temporary structures known as pandals that house idols of the goddess Durga. The incident occurred at the exit gate in Kolkata's Girish Park area after heavy rain led to overcrowding as large numbers of devotees attempted to leave the venue, local TV said. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's office, in a post on social media platform X, announced a compensation payment of 200,000 rupees ($2,106.15) for the next of kin of those who died and 50,000 rupees each for the injured. ($1 = 94.9600 Indian rupees)

item.title: Explosion at Iraqi paramilitary alliance base kills one member, sources say
item.description: An explosion at the Popular Mobilisation Forces headquarters in Baghdad killed one member of the Iraqi paramilitary group and wounded four others, according to a security and a medical source.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An explosion at the Popular Mobilisation Forces headquarters in Baghdad killed one member of the Iraqi paramilitary group and wounded four others, according to a security and a medical source. The group said a stockpile of obsolete ammunition had exploded, injuring five people and causing a fire, which has since been brought under control. The PMF, known in Arabic as Hashd al-Shaabi, is an umbrella group of mostly Shi'ite paramilitary factions that has been formally integrated into Iraq's state security forces and includes several groups aligned with Iran.

item.title: Czech PM Babis suffers setback in Senate elections
item.description: Leading Czech opposition parties won the most votes in Senate elections on Saturday, while Prime Minister Andrej Babis' party failed to secure any of the seats it contested in one of its first big electoral tests since taking power last year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Leading Czech opposition parties won the most votes in Senate elections on Saturday, while Prime Minister Andrej Babis' party failed to secure any of the seats it contested in one of its first big electoral tests since taking power last year. Babis' ANO party had hoped to make gains in the 81-seat upper house, where one-third of seats were up for election and opposition parties hold a majority. Babis described the result as "catastrophic", but the outcome is unlikely to destabilise his eurosceptic coalition government, which includes right-wing and far-right parties. Since taking office, the government has ended direct state military support for Ukraine in its war with Russia and challenged European Union climate policies. The lower house remains the country's main legislative chamber and can override Senate vetoes, limiting the upper chamber's ability to block government legislation. The Senate nevertheless plays an important role in approving constitutional changes, confirming presidential nominees to the Constitutional Court and electing its own speaker, the country's second-highest state official after the president. Despite the setback, ANO continues to lead national opinion polls. The government has loosened fiscal policy to boost wages, pensions and transport investment, drawing criticism in the traditionally frugal country of 10.9 million people. Turnout in run-off voting for Senate seats on Friday and Saturday was low, following the first round last weekend. Under the electoral system, the top two candidates advance to a run-off unless one secures more than 50% of the vote in the first round. The pro-European Mayors and Independents party emerged as the strongest performer, winning 10 of the 14 seats it contested, including two secured outright in the first round. The Civic Democrats won seven seats. The vote followed municipal elections last weekend in which ANO won six of the country's 13 regional capitals, down from eight four years ago.

item.title: Cofundador da Anthropic afirma que impacto da IA acelera rapidamente e pode impulsionar PIB dos EUA
item.description: O rápido avanço das capacidades da inteligência artificial trará mudanças muito mais rápidas em todas as áreas, afirmou neste sábado o cofundador da Anthropic, Jack Clark, com um dos modelos econômicos internos da empresa prevendo que isso poderia ampliar significativamente a produção econômica dos EUA para US$44 trilhões até 2030.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O rápido avanço das capacidades da inteligência artificial trará mudanças muito mais rápidas em todas as áreas, afirmou neste sábado o cofundador da Anthropic, Jack Clark, com um dos modelos econômicos internos da empresa prevendo que isso poderia ampliar significativamente a produção econômica dos EUA para US$44 trilhões até 2030. Em discurso nas reuniões anuais do FMI e do Banco Mundial em Bangcoc, Clark disse que é necessária uma cooperação internacional para estabelecer “regras incomuns e rigorosas” para essa tecnologia transformadora. Clark disse que o número de US$44 trilhões, que se compara ao nível atual de pouco mais de US$30 trilhões, “parece muito absurdo”, mas a IA está aumentando enormemente as descobertas científicas. “Eu sei, mas isso decorre da premissa de que a tecnologia continuará melhorando. E se o PIB crescesse tanto assim, a doutrina econômica sugere que novas indústrias e invenções precisariam ter sido criadas para impulsionar uma expansão econômica tão significativa.” (Reportagem de David Lawder)

item.title: Membros do FMI pedem mais apoio em meio a impactos de guerras e a riscos da “inteligência avançada”
item.description: Os países membros do Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI) pediram um aumento do apoio aos países que enfrentam desafios de financiamento de curto prazo causados por repercussões negativas decorrentes de guerras e dos altos preços da energia, e afirmaram que os riscos econômicos continuam inclinados para o lado negativo.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder
item.content:encoded: Os países membros do Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI) pediram um aumento do apoio aos países que enfrentam desafios de financiamento de curto prazo causados por repercussões negativas decorrentes de guerras e dos altos preços da energia, e afirmaram que os riscos econômicos continuam inclinados para o lado negativo. E, embora tenha havido um impulso aos investimentos e ao comércio por meio das “tecnologias de inteligência avançada”, elas também acarretam riscos, afirmou o presidente do Comitê Monetário e Financeiro Internacional em um comunicado após uma reunião em Bangcoc. “A escalada de conflitos e tensões comerciais pode perturbar ainda mais rotas comerciais essenciais, agravar as pressões sobre os preços das commodities, inclusive dos produtos energéticos refinados, e piorar a segurança energética e alimentar”, afirmou o comunicado divulgado pelo ministro das Finanças da Arábia Saudita, Mohammed Al-Jadaan, presidente do IMFC. O IMFC é o principal comitê diretor do fundo de crédito para crises, que conta com 191 membros. Al-Jadaan disse à Reuters que o texto do comunicado foi acordado por todos os membros. No início desta semana, os Estados Unidos estavam pressionando outros membros do FMI para que renomeassem a inteligência artificial como “superinteligência” no comunicado, em consonância com o nome preferido pelo presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, para a tecnologia, disse uma [USN:L1N4610GV TEXT:"autoridade de alto escalão do Tesouro dos EUA à Reuters"]. A versão final da declaração do presidente do IMFC não continha nenhuma referência à inteligência artificial. A declaração afirmou que o impacto incerto das “tecnologias de inteligência avançada”, juntamente com a alta dos rendimentos dos títulos nas principais economias, que se transmite para países com elevado endividamento, "pode ampliar as vulnerabilidades macrofinanceiras". “As rápidas mudanças tecnológicas, as transformações demográficas, a maior frequência de eventos climáticos extremos e desastres naturais, bem como a fragmentação geoeconômica, estão agravando os dilemas de política pública”, afirmava a declaração. As economias membros concordaram em apoiar os países que empreendem reformas e lidam com vulnerabilidades relacionadas à dívida, com atenção especial aos países de baixa renda e de renda média vulneráveis, bem como aos Estados afetados por conflitos. “Incentivamos o aumento do apoio a países com dívida sustentável e uma agenda sólida de reformas e promoção do crescimento, mas que enfrentam desafios de financiamento de curto prazo”, afirma o comunicado, observando que vários membros garantiram apoio ao Fundo de Redução da Pobreza e Crescimento do FMI, que apoia países pobres e em desenvolvimento. (Reportagem de David Lawder)

item.title: Spain's hard left fails to unite before election, hurting chances of staying in power
item.description: Spain's hard-left parties on Saturday presented separate candidate lists for a snap election after talks on a nationwide pact collapsed, reducing Socialist prime minister Pedro Sanchez' chances of staying in power at the head of a leftist coalition.
item.dc:creator: David Latona
item.content:encoded: Spain's hard-left parties on Saturday presented separate candidate lists for a [USN:L8N45R05N TEXT:"snap election"] after talks on a nationwide pact collapsed, reducing Socialist prime minister Pedro Sanchez' chances of staying in power at the head of a leftist coalition. Spain's electoral system disadvantages smaller parties running separately, particularly in less populous provinces, where fewer seats are available. The division could also demoralise left-wing voters, whom organisers hoped to galvanise around [USN:L1N45U0F8 TEXT:"housing protests"] and [USN:L8N3WQ1QB TEXT:"fear of the far right"]. The Broad Front, a platform comprising several parties represented in the minority government, and the other main party on the hard left, Podemos ("We Can"), had been publicly arguing over the leading positions on joint candidate lists for the November 29 election in Madrid and Barcelona, the largest constituencies. Long-standing [USN:L8N3650H2 TEXT:"animosities"] between former comrades-turned-rivals did not help. "These past few days have been very difficult ... some people will be disappointed today, and for that I am sorry," Ada Colau, the former Barcelona mayor and leader of the Broad Front, said at her platform's launch event in Madrid. Podemos, whose lead candidate is former equality minister Irene Montero, had proposed open primaries to determine candidates' positions on joint lists. But the Broad Front refused, arguing there was too little time, and wanted its own preferred candidates to lead the lists in Madrid and Barcelona. Podemos then made a separate pact deal with the Republican Left of Catalonia (ERC), which favours Catalan independence.

item.title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinians, European diplomats in West Bank, Belgium says
item.description: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian civilians, European diplomats and a French mayor in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, Belgium's foreign minister said, a day after settlers beat an American photojournalist.
item.dc:creator: Ali Sawafta, Mohammed Torokman
item.content:encoded: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian civilians, European diplomats and a French mayor in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, Belgium's foreign minister said, a day after settlers beat an [USN:L8N4620II TEXT:"American photojournalist"]. Maxime Prevot said Belgium's consul general to the Palestinians, French and Polish diplomats, and Catholic representatives were among those attacked. A Belgian vehicle was also damaged, he said. "As the occupying power, Israeli authorities must protect Palestinians, ensure the safety of diplomats and journalists, and bring those responsible to justice. Impunity for violent settlers must end," Prevot said in a statement posted on X. 'THROWN TO THE GROUND' Bernard Baudoux, mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France, told Reuters he had been harvesting olives near the Palestinian Christian village of Taybeh in solidarity with the local community when he was "violently attacked" by masked settlers. "I was thrown to the ground," he said. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned the attack, describing the perpetrators as Israeli rioters. He also suggested the diplomats should have coordinated their visit with the Israeli military. "Such coordination could have helped safeguard the visitors’ security," he said in a statement on X. Palestinian Vice President Hussein al-Sheikh condemned the attack, calling it a small example of the "daily terrorism" to which Palestinians are subjected. Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, have periodically condemned settler violence, while saying it is carried out by a small minority. Palestinians and human rights groups dispute that characterisation. ISRAELI POLICE OPEN INVESTIGATION Settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank have surged over the past three years. Journalists, activists and foreign observers have also been targeted. On Friday, dozens of masked settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives in the West Bank. Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine, a US citizen covering the harvest, was hospitalised after being assaulted by masked settlers. "Palestinians face this violence every day. Settlers also target journalists reporting on it and diplomats. Harvesting olives, reporting the news or carrying out diplomatic duties should never put anyone at risk of attack," Prevot said. Belgium, which has announced a ban on imports from Israeli settlements in the West Bank and the Golan Heights, will press for European Union sanctions "against those responsible for this violence and those who support them," he added. Polish Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maciej Wewior said on X that a convoy carrying diplomats, including Polish officials, had been attacked. The Polish diplomats were unharmed. "Attacks on members of the diplomatic corps are absolutely unacceptable," he said. Israeli police said they had opened an investigation into the incident. There was no immediate announcement of any arrests. Prosecutions of settlers accused of violent crimes against Palestinians in the West Bank are rare.

item.title: Bayern crush Leipzig 6-1 to live up to coach Kompany's prediction
item.description: Bayern Munich obliterated RB Leipzig 6-1 on Saturday with a scintillating performance, to live up to coach Vincent Kompany's prediction before the game that his team was close to hitting top form.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bayern Munich obliterated RB Leipzig 6-1 on Saturday with a scintillating performance, to live up to coach Vincent Kompany's prediction before the game that his team was close to hitting top form. Kompany had said on Friday his team's consecutive draws in the league and Europe were [USN:L6N4620HY TEXT:"not representative"] of Bayern's current level and his players proved him right, delivering a statement win, with Luis Diaz hitting a hat-trick, to silence critics. The Bavarians had drawn 2-2 against Augsburg while also conceding the [USN:L6N45W03O TEXT:"fastest"] goal in Bundesliga history last week before a shock 3-3 [USN:L6N45Z15P TEXT:"draw"] at outsiders Viking in the Champions League on Tuesday. They had to come from behind in both those matches but against Leipzig it was clear from the start who was boss. Bayern opened their account with Diaz in the 12th minute before the Colombian set up Aleksandar Pavlovic for their second 14 minutes later. Michael Olise, who had terrorised the Leipzig defence in the first half, capped his outstanding performance with a goal in the 34th. Diaz bagged his hat-trick with goals either side of Harry Kane's tap-in on the England captain's 100th Bundesliga appearance. Leipzig scored a late consolation goal in stoppage time. The result lifted the champions into top spot on 14 points, ahead of Borussia Dortmund on goal difference, after the Ruhr valley club slipped up with a goalless draw at Union Berlin. Dortmund, who lost 1-0 in the Champions League at Bodo/Glimt on Wednesday and have now failed to win any of their last three matches across all competitions, lacked spark. They also had striker Konstantinos Karetsas, who had come on in the 62nd minute, go off with an ankle injury just eight minutes later. He had come back after collapsing in September during a Champions League game due to what the club said were 'circulatory problems'. The visitors had to settle for a second consecutive league draw. Freiburg, on 13, are in action against Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday and can reclaim top spot with a win. Werder Bremen became the first Bundesliga team in history to come back from a two-goal deficit in three consecutive league matches when they did it against Paderborn for a 2-2 draw.

item.title: Report: Florida QB Tramell Jones Jr. to start vs. Texas
item.description: Florida quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. will make his first career start on Saturday at No. 7 Texas, ESPN reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Florida quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. will make his first career start on Saturday at No. 7 Texas, ESPN reported. The sophomore takes over for Aaron Philo, who is dealing with a shoulder injury and could be available as an emergency backup when the Gators (4-2, 2-2 SEC) visit the Longhorns (4-1, 1-1) in Austin. Jones replaced Philo in the fourth quarter in last Saturday's 38-19 home loss to South Carolina and threw for 40 yards with one interception. Jones has completed 44 of 64 passes for 443 yards with four touchdowns and two interceptions in seven games over the past two seasons at Florida. --Field Level Media

item.title: Wizards monitoring top overall pick AJ Dybantsa (ankle)
item.description: No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa sustained a mild ankle sprain during the Washington Wizards' preseason finale against the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday, head coach Brian Keefe announced.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa sustained a mild ankle sprain during the Washington Wizards' preseason finale against the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday, head coach Brian Keefe announced. Keefe told sideline reporter Chase Hughes the rookie forward was removed from the game as a precaution and will undergo further testing. "We'll look at it more when we get more information," Keefe said. Dybantsa landed awkwardly and fell to the court following a midrange jumper and limped to the locker room. He scored 12 points in 15 minutes before exiting in the second quarter of the 107-106 setback to New Orleans. The Wizards open the regular season Wednesday against the visiting Milwaukee Bucks. The 6-foot-9 Dybantsa led the nation in scoring at 25.5 points per game during his lone college campaign at BYU. --Field Level Media

item.title: Huracán Trudy se fortalece ligeramente frente a costas del Pacífico mexicano
item.description: El huracán Trudy se fortaleció ligeramente el sábado en aguas del Pacífico mexicano, aunque se espere que se debilite a partir del domingo, mientras avanza hacia el noroeste y se acercaría más tarde a la costa del suroeste y centro de México, afectada por lluvias en las últimas semanas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El huracán Trudy se fortaleció ligeramente el sábado en aguas del Pacífico mexicano, aunque se espere que se debilite a partir del domingo, mientras avanza hacia el noroeste y se acercaría más tarde a la costa del suroeste y centro de México, afectada por lluvias en las últimas semanas. Trudy, categoría 1en la escala de Saffir-Simpson, se ubicaba a 425 kilómetros al oeste del puerto turístico Acapulco, en el estado Guerrero, y soplaba vientos máximos sostenidos de 150 kilómetros por hora (km/h), mientras se movía a 17 km/h, de acuerdo al reporte más reciente del Centro Nacional de Huracanes de Estados Unidos (NHC, por su sigla en inglés). El aviso de huracán estaba vigente para la costa desde el sur de Manzanillo, en el estado Colima, hasta Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco, en el occidente de México. El NHC dijo que se espera que Trudy descargue lluvias de entre 10 a 20 centímetros a lo largo y cerca de la costa de Michoacán, Colima y Jalisco. "Esta lluvia puede producir inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra que amenazan la vida, especialmente a lo largo de un terreno empinado", señala el reporte. La estatal Comisión Nacional del Agua (Conagua) en México advirtió también que las precipitaciones generadas por Trudy, que llegó a ser un huracán categoría 3, podrían provocar desbordamientos e inundaciones en zonas bajas en las zonas involucradas. En las últimas semanas, la costa del Pacífico mexicano ha sido golpeada por los huracanes[USN:L6N45L0YK TEXT:" Polo"] y[USN:L8N45V0SM TEXT:" Simon,"] y la tormenta Rachel. Debido a las inundaciones, al menos ocho personas perdieron la vida en la ciudad costera de Ensenada, en el estado Baja California.

item.title: Kenya confirms four new Ebola cases, bringing total number to seven
item.description: Kenya confirmed four new cases of the Ebola Bundibugyo virus on Saturday, including three health workers who treated the country's first patient, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to seven, the health ministry said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kenya confirmed four new cases of the Ebola Bundibugyo virus on Saturday, including three health workers who treated the country's first patient, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to seven, the health ministry said. The other new case is a male relative of the index patient, who died. The relative had been in quarantine since October 6, the ministry said in a statement. The cases are the first known infections passed on inside Kenya, where the first patient arrived from Congo on October 3. But the ministry says it has traced and quarantined nearly all of his contacts and there is no evidence that the virus is spreading in the community. The three health workers — two men and a woman aged 29, 35 and 32 respectively — managed the index case on October 3 and 4 and had been in quarantine since October 9, it said. All four new patients were already in quarantine when they developed symptoms and were diagnosed. The second and third patients [USN:L8N4621HW TEXT:"confirmed earlier"] are stable and responding well to supportive treatment, the ministry said. It said 128 of 130 listed contacts, or 98.5%, had been traced and placed in quarantine, higher than the 85% global benchmark it said was needed to break the chain of transmission. Kenya's cases are linked to the Ebola epidemic in Congo — [USN:L8N45Z1AX TEXT:"the second-largest"] outbreak ever recorded, with more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,000 deaths. There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola. The [USN:L8N45S0GY TEXT:"first Kenyan case "]was a man who had been ill in Congo for about a month before travelling by road to Uganda and flying to Nairobi on October 3. He died on October 5. His arrival has raised concerns about screening at the Congo-Uganda border, which has been closed since May, and at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport. Efforts to trace the remaining two contacts were ongoing, the ministry said. "The risk to the general public remains low as there is no evidence of community transmission," it said, adding that there were no restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings.

item.title: Zelenskiy critica dispensa de sanções à Rússia por Trump como "equivocada"
item.description: A decisão do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, de conceder uma isenção de sanções e tarifas contra a Rússia poucos dias antes da entrada em vigor levará "infelizmente" a um alívio adicional para Moscou e incentivará novas agressões russas, disse o presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, neste sábado.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh, Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: A decisão do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, de conceder uma isenção de sanções e tarifas contra a Rússia poucos dias antes da entrada em vigor levará "infelizmente" a um alívio adicional para Moscou e incentivará novas agressões russas, disse o presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, neste sábado. "A decisão de desfazer tudo isso, de bloquear tudo isso, me parece equivocada", escreveu Zelenskiy na rede social X. "Isso certamente ajuda apenas os russos." Um decreto assinado por Trump na noite de sexta-feira concedeu uma isenção a importantes sanções e tarifas dos EUA relacionadas à Rússia, incluindo tarifas sobre produtos russos e penalidades para a compra de petróleo e gás do país, que estavam programadas para entrar em vigor na próxima semana sob a legislação conhecida como Lei Graham, sancionada por ele no mês passado. Trump afirmou que a isenção atende aos interesses nacionais dos Estados Unidos. A lei tinha como objetivo aumentar a pressão sobre a Rússia por causa da invasão da Ucrânia , que começou em 2022. Trump, no entanto, vem se mostrando mais favorável a Moscou, ao mesmo tempo em que critica publicamente o presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, chegando a sugerir que Kiev precisa de um novo líder. Zelenskiy afirmou que a mais recente medida de Trump fortalece a posição do presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, e incentiva novos ataques da Rússia. "Isso apenas alimenta sua satisfação e seu desejo de continuar matando pessoas", escreveu Zelenskiy, acrescentando que a Rússia atingiu na sexta-feira mais de 15 instalações ucranianas de geração e transmissão de energia. "Isso certamente não põe fim à guerra." O líder ucraniano também acusou a Rússia de planejar intensificar os ataques no oeste da Ucrânia. "A Rússia está se preparando para isso? Eu acredito que sim", escreveu Zelenskiy. Kirill Dmitriev, enviado russo para investimentos, afirmou na sexta-feira que a isenção concedida por Trump representa "um momento verdadeiramente histórico". Em publicação no X, ele disse que, caso as penalidades tivessem entrado em vigor, poderiam ter interrompido de forma efetiva toda a cooperação econômica entre a Rússia e os Estados Unidos. Semanas antes das eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA, nas quais os republicanos de Trump lutam para manter seu estreito controle sobre ambas as câmaras do Congresso, as novas medidas poderiam ter corrido o risco de [USN:L6N45A18J TEXT:"elevar"] ainda mais [USN:L6N45A18J TEXT:"os preços do petróleo"] , enquanto os norte-americanos enfrentam custos crescentes atribuídos em grande parte à guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã, segundo analistas. A [USN:L6N45A18J TEXT:"legislação,"] cujo principal apoiador no Congresso foi o falecido senador Lindsey Graham, republicano da Carolina do Sul, teria imposto tarifas de até 100% em 30 dias sobre todas as mercadorias trazidas aos EUA dos cinco maiores importadores de petróleo bruto ou gás russo, bem como por qualquer país que, conscientemente, comprasse petróleo ou gás 30 dias após a promulgação da lei ou estivesse entre os cinco principais países que ajudassem a Rússia a contornar as sanções. O decreto diz que a isenção permanecerá em vigor até que Trump ou seus principais assessores determinem que “outras medidas sejam apropriadas”. Trump assinou a Lei Lindsey O. Graham de Sanções à Rússia e ao Irã de 2026 em meados de setembro. “Apresentei ao Congresso uma certificação de que a emissão dessa isenção neste momento é do interesse nacional dos Estados Unidos”, afirmou Trump na ordem. Países como a China e [USN:L1N45G03K TEXT:"a Índia"], que estão entre os maiores compradores de petróleo russo, manifestaram preocupações em relação ao projeto de sanções contra a Rússia. (Reportagem de Kanishka Singh, Jasper Ward e Patricia Zengerle, em Washington; Reportagem adicional de Gleb Bryanski, em Moscou, e Laila Kearney, em Nova York)

item.title: Yes Bank Q2 profit rises but AT1 ruling not booked as further appeal weighed
item.description: Yes Bank on Saturday reported a 65% jump in second-quarter profit to 10.80 billion Indian rupees ($114 million), but said the figure does not reflect the impact of a Supreme Court ruling this week that set aside its 2020 write-off of 84 billion rupees ($884 million) of additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds.
item.dc:creator: Ashwin Manikandan
item.content:encoded: Yes Bank (YESB.NS) on Saturday reported a 65% jump in second-quarter profit to 10.80 billion Indian rupees ($114 million), but said the figure does not reflect the impact of a Supreme Court ruling this week that set aside its 2020 write-off of 84 billion rupees ($884 million) of additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds. Had the impact been recognised, the bank would have posted a quarterly loss of 52.17 billion rupees, it said in a filing. The Supreme Court on Thursday [USN:L4N4610S4 TEXT:"upheld"] a 2023 Bombay High Court judgment that set aside the write-down, dismissing appeals by the lender, the Reserve Bank of India and the federal government. The Mumbai-based lender, in which Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation [RIC:RIC:SUMFDS.UL] holds a 24.99% stake, said it was evaluating the implications, including the manner and timing of implementation. It is also weighing "all legal remedies available", including further proceedings before the Supreme Court. The figures are indicative and subject to revision, the bank said. If they were adjusted to reflect the court ruling, the bank's net worth would fall to 469.70 billion rupees from 532.68 billion, and borrowings would rise to 861.49 billion rupees from 777.34 billion, it said. Its total capital adequacy ratio would stay unaffected at 14.5%, the bank said. It had said in a filing on Friday that its common equity tier-1 ratio would decline about 250 basis points. AT1 bonds are high-risk debt instruments that can be written off or converted into equity when a bank comes under financial stress. Yes Bank, a mid-sized lender, was rescued in 2020 under a restructuring scheme that brought in new investors. The bonds were written off by an administrator in charge of the restructuring. Analysts had forecast a profit of 9.55 billion rupees, according to LSEG data. The bank's net interest income rose 22.7% to 28.22 billion rupees. Advances grew 23.7% from a year earlier and deposits rose 19.5%. Provisions for bad loans and other contingencies fell 24.2% to 3.17 billion rupees. Other income rose 14.4% to 18.82 billion rupees. The gross non-performing asset ratio was 1.2% at end-September, against 1.3% at end-June. ($1 = 94.9600 Indian rupees)

item.title: High debt, growing strains put focus on need for new development approaches
item.description: High debt levels, rising debt-service costs and a sharp drop in official development assistance are forcing developing countries and institutions that help them to rethink development and look for new sources of funding, including from the private sector.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal, Rae Wee
item.content:encoded: High debt levels, rising debt-service costs and a sharp drop in official development assistance are forcing developing countries and institutions that help them to rethink development and look for new sources of funding, including from the private sector. World Bank President Ajay Banga, who has led a drive that has more than tripled the [USN:L1N4580ZW TEXT:"private capital"] flowing to development projects since 2022, told the annual IMF and World Bank meetings that changes were needed to help countries address headwinds posed by persistent conflicts, a drop in official development assistance and rising debt burdens. A huge demographic challenge was also unfolding, he said, with some 1.2 billion young people likely to join the job market in the next 10 to 15 years, but only 400 million jobs in sight. The answer, Banga said, would depend on bringing public finance, private investment, philanthropy and technology together to meet each country's needs. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said he would make [USN:L1N4600EL TEXT:"debt restructuring"] and other help for the poorest countries a key theme for Britain's upcoming G20 presidency. But he said the private sector needed to step up since Britain and other rich nations could not provide the same level of support as during the last big debt forgiveness push at the turn of the millennium. "The risks of lending to emerging markets have been overestimated and the risk of default has been overestimated," he told a panel on Wednesday hosted by the Rockefeller Foundation, a private US foundation that works on development. Developing countries are also looking for answers outside the two Bretton Woods institutions, disappointed by the response to high debt levels, climate change, worsening inequality and geopolitical challenges. "The world has, in many ways, changed for the worse since 2023," Shekhar Aiyar, director and chief executive of the Indian Council for Research on International Economic Relations, told an event hosted by the Center for Global Development this week. "Developing countries have been caught in a downward spiral of decelerating growth and increased vulnerability ... at the same time, there has been a vast scaling back of bilateral aid." International aid from OECD Development Assistance Committee donor countries fell 23% in real terms in 2025, marking the biggest annual drop in the history of ODA. The top five donors — the US, Germany, UK, Japan and France — all cut aid, together accounting for 96% of the total drop. Meanwhile, according to UNCTAD — the official UN body responsible for trade, investment and development issues — developing countries' combined external debt stock reached $12.3 trillion in the same year, up by half a trillion from 2024. NEW PARTNERSHIPS AND APPROACHES US President Donald Trump's sweeping tariffs have added to strains and prompted many developing countries and emerging markets to forge new trade partnerships that do not include the United States. Indian Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman told an Atlantic Council broadcast that countries like hers were plowing ahead with more bilateral partnerships. "I feel this approach of 'Yes, we want multilateralism, but yet we're not waiting for it, we are going ahead with bilateral,' has really rewarded India," Sitharaman said. Eric LeCompte, executive director of Jubilee USA Network, which advocates for debt relief, said this year's meetings were a big disappointment for developing countries, providing no new initiative to help those already facing steep debt-service payments and now saddled with soaring borrowing costs. He said the IMF failed to reach critical mass to launch its expanded Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust, which lends to low-income countries at low interest rates, and barely mentioned its Catastrophe Containment and Relief Trust, which provides grants for debt relief to the world's poorest countries. "There was a lot of information about how challenging problems are, but we saw hardly any action," he said, aside from tweaks to debt restructuring plans by the Global Sovereign Debt Roundtable. "We were expecting more," he said. Jean Saldanha, director of the European Network on Debt and Development, asked: "Where are the emergency measures to stop countries in the Global South being forced to spend more on debt than on health and education? And where are the serious policy responses to the escalating climate emergency, boosted by a Super El Niño?" "The least-developed countries have said loud and clear they need more climate grants, less debt, simpler access and faster disbursements," she said. Muhammad Al Jasser, who chairs the Islamic Development Bank group, told Reuters there was growing interest in securing private sector funds to augment increasingly scarce public resources. "The challenges are huge. We're not going to solve them either single-handedly or even collectively in a short period of time, but I think we are (heading) in the right direction," he said, adding his bank was aiming to deploy $10 billion in financing next year.

item.title: Australia still undecided on starting XI for second test v S Africa
item.description: Australia are assessing all selection options ahead of the second test against South Africa in Gqeberha on Sunday as they look to claim the three-match test series following a thumping 214-run win in the opening game.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia are assessing all selection options ahead of the second test against South Africa in Gqeberha on Sunday as they look to claim the three-match test series following a thumping 214-run win in the opening game. All-rounder Cameron Green will miss out again with an abdominal strain but wicketkeeper-batter Josh Inglis could win his race to recover from a finger injury. Whether he would start if fit remains to be seen, as Australia also ponder an all seam bowling attack that would leave out experienced spinner Nathan Lyon. With bad weather expected on the first two days there is a chance that the game could be shortened, or that conditions would be heavily weighted in favour of the seamers. "We always look at all options," captain Pat Cummins told reporters on Saturday. "We love playing with Nath. We saw last week, (he took) a couple of key wickets in the first innings. And even the control he gives. It makes the rest of us fast bowlers be able to function around him." He suggested that Matt Renshaw, who scored 190 and 82 in the first test in Durban, would remain as a middle order batter, rather than an option to open the innings as he has done before. "After what Renners did last week, I presume he'll stay at number five," Cummins said. "What he deserved even more credit for is that we'd asked him to do a different role and he just said straight away 'yep, no worries, whatever the team needs'. "There were so many positives in addition to the runs he scored last week. He was a delight, and really helped me and Lyon get through those partnerships (with Renshaw)." South Africa lead the head-to-head in Gqeberha 4-3, with Australia’s last victory there coming in 1997.

item.title: Egypt's Sisi seeks parliament's backing to help defend Saudi Arabia if asked
item.description: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday Egypt would take any measures necessary to defend Saudi Arabia if asked, amid escalating Houthi attacks on the kingdom, and parliament announced an emergency session on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
